0.long_answer: The most common form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia is due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency, which primarily leads to a deficiency of cortisol. Cortisol is a crucial glucocorticoid hormone produced by the adrenal cortex, and its deficiency is a central aspect of this condition. The synthetic analog of cortisol, known as hydrocortisone, is one of the most prescribed medications due to its wide usage in various clinical settings, including as an anti-inflammatory and in hormone replacement therapy.
